subject: Request: temporary completion buffer for nightly async jobs
messages:
From: Ryan Wu <ryan.wu@fintechco.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: 2025-06-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary completion buffer for nightly async jobs

Aisha / Marcus,

Thanks again for last week's onboarding walkthrough. We're seeing one recurring issue with our nightly reprocessing pipeline: when downstream jobs overlap with spikes in upstream data (typically after 02:00 PST), a subset of asynchronous inference jobs regularly exceed the current 2-hour completion SLA.

Impact summary:
- ~0.8% of nightly batches currently finish in 2–6 hours during peak backfills.
- When jobs run long we have to delay reconciliation and downstream reporting, which pushes our nightly SLA internally and cascades to other teams.

We'd like to request a temporary completion buffer on the Redwood SLA for these specific nightly async jobs while we roll a fix on our side (expected 6–8 weeks). Proposed constraints from our side:
- Jobs will include a stable request_id/idempotency key on every submission.
- We will tag batch jobs with "finance-nightly" and a run_id so you can scope the carve-out.

What we'd like from Redwood:
1) A temporary extension of the batch completion window for tagged nightly jobs from 2 hours to up to 6 hours for a time-limited period (Q3).
2) Clear retry/credit rules (how credits apply if completion exceeds 4 hours, and what happens beyond 6 hours).
3) Technical guardrails: idempotency guidance and any recommended retry/backoff best-practices.

Attached a small sample of the run metadata and one failing job trace (run-sample.csv). We're happy to share more logs if needed.

Can you let us know what documentation or contract language Procurement would need to move forward?

Thanks,

Ryan
Ryan Wu
Director, Data Platform
FinTechCo
ryan.wu@fintechco.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary completion buffer for nightly async jobs

Ryan — thanks for the clear summary and the sample. We can support a scoped, time-limited amendment to the batch completion window while you execute the fix. To keep this operationally safe for both sides, here are three options we recommend (short form):

Option A — Temporary completion buffer (recommended):
- Scope: tag = "finance-nightly" and run_id.
- Completion window: 6 hours for nightly tagged jobs during the 8-week remediation period.
- Credit policy: 30% service credit for jobs that finish between 4–6 hours (applies to affected unit charges), full credit threshold if >6 hours.
- Required guardrails: idempotency key (request_id) present on every submitted task; idempotency TTL = 72 hours; sequence number for multi-part batches.

Option B — Keep 2h SLA but allow queued backfill lane on Dedicated capacity for the same price + limited buffer: requires Dedicated commitment.

Option C — Maintain SLA but carve out explicit maintenance windows (2x/week) where longer runtimes are allowed and excluded from SLA calculations.

Operational notes:
- We can add a run-level flag so our routing layer pins tagged jobs to a lower-priority batch pool with longer timeouts and different retry semantics.
- Marcus has suggested an idempotency + dedupe policy that avoids duplicate scoring when clients retry within the TTL. I'm attaching a short amendment draft (slo-amend-proposal.pdf) and a compact spec for idempotency expectations (idempotency-spec.txt).

Next steps: if Procurement agrees to Option A we can draft an SLA amendment and route it through legal + DocuSign. Marcus, any technical caveats to add?

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman

Subject: Re: Request: temporary completion buffer for nightly async jobs

A quick technical note / proposed safe defaults — adding for record and to ensure the amendment is implementable without changing core runtime code:

1) Idempotency + dedupe
- Acceptable idempotency key: string up to 128 chars (request_id).
- TTL: 72 hours for keys; dedupe is per model+client+key.
- Multi-piece batches should include sequence number and total_parts so our reassembly is deterministic.

2) Retry semantics
- Client-side: exponential backoff starting at 10s, max backoff 30m, max retries 10.
- Server-side: for tagged nightly jobs we will allow extended server-side lease up to 6 hours; after 6 hours job state -> "failed:expiry".
- Retries that arrive with the same request_id within TTL will be deduplicated; arrival after TTL is treated as new job.

3) Safe-retry handshake token (optional)
- We can offer an optional short-lived handshake token for long-running jobs so clients can query progress without creating retry noise. TTL 1 hour; issued per run_id.

4) Observability & reconciliation
- We will emit a per-run event to your CloudWatch/Historical API with: run_id, partition, submitted_at, started_at, finished_at, final_status, request_id.

5) Mitigation to reduce long-tail
- Enable prefix-KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes in the nightly pipeline; reduces cold-KV misses and long-tail outliers.

I'll attach the ops runbook with the exact event names and the patch notes for the temporary routing change (ops-runbook.xlsx). If Procurement needs wording for contract language I can produce the exact amendment clause.

— Marcus

Aisha / Ryan,

Thanks for the proposal and the technical details. We reviewed internally and Procurement is prepared to accept Option A (temporary completion buffer to 6 hours) with the following conditions:

- The scope must be limited to jobs tagged "finance-nightly" with explicit run_id and request_id as described.
- Redwood must provide the observability events Marcus referenced so we can reconcile billing and failures.
- Service credit: 30% credit for affected units finishing between 4–6 hours; if a job exceeds 6 hours it will be considered a breach and escalated per contract.

Please send us a short contract amendment (statement of work) and the DocuSign packet. We will countersign as soon as Legal verifies the clause. Also include the idempotency and retry language verbatim so our engineers can align.
